# The lock will not let this slot be written, or will not clear it.
    SLOT_REFUSED = "slot_refused"
    # The lock answered with a failure that may not repeat.
    TRANSIENT = "transient"
    # No answer from the lock: a disconnect, a timeout, or a service in front
    # of it answering in its place.
    NO_ANSWER = "no_answer"
    # The lock already holds what was asked.
    ALREADY_SO = "already_so"


def _ms(start: float) -> float:
    """Return the milliseconds since ``start`` on the monotonic clock (for logs)."""
    return (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000


def _where(slot: int | None, slots: tuple[int, ...]) -> Any:
    """Return the slot, or slots, an exchange or job is about (for logs)."""
    return slots[0] if len(slots) == 1 else slots or slot


class LockError(Exception):
    """A failed exchange: what kind, and whether it reached the lock."""

    def __init__(
        self, kind: ErrorKind, *, sent: bool = True, message: str = "", cause: str = ""
    ) -> None:
        """
        Describe the failure; ``sent`` is False when nothing left for the lock.

        ``cause`` is set only when the provider named, for the user, why it
        failed.
        """
        super().__init__(message or kind.value)
        self.kind = kind
        self.sent = sent
        self.message = message
        self.cause = cause


class LockPort(Protocol):
    """What the worker needs from a provider."""

    async def read(self, slots: Collection[int]) -> Mapping[int, Reading]:
        """
        Return what the lock says about each of ``slots`` now; raise ``LockError``.

        Never a cache: a write is checked by reading its slot back, and a
        cached old value would count against a write that worked (#873,
        #1090). A provider that cannot read the lock itself leaves the slot
        out, and the write is trusted. Cached views come in as pushes.
        """
        ...

    async def write(self, slot: int, pin: str | None) -> bool | None:
        """
        Put ``pin`` in ``slot``, or clear it for None; raise ``LockError``.

        False when the lock answered that there was nothing to change -- a
        clear that found nothing: that says nothing about what the slot holds.
        """
        ...


@dataclass
class _Job:
    kind: str
    slot: int | None = None
    slots: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    # Held slots a read also asks about, each on its own (``_read_held``).
    held: tuple[int, ...] = ()
    reading: Reading | None = None
    # When a push was taken in: dropped if its slot was written since.
    seq: int = 0
    done: asyncio.Future[Any] | None = None
    # A turn's exchange, made by someone else's provider.
    call: Callable[[], Awaitable[Any]] | None = None


def _resolve(
    done: asyncio.Future[Any] | None,
    result: Any = None,
    error: BaseException | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Answer a caller's future, unless the caller has given up on it."""
    if done is None or done.done():
        return
    if error is not None:
        done.set_exception(error)
    else:
        done.set_result(result)


@dataclass
class LockWorker[P: LockPort]:
    """The one owner of a lock's slots and of every exchange with it."""

    port: P
    salt: bytes
    gap: float = 2.0
    # Seconds one exchange may take before it counts as no answer.
    budget: float = 60.0
    clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    sleep: Callable[[float], Awaitable[None]] = asyncio.sleep
    on_change: Callable[[], None] = lambda: None
    # A write is about to be sent: what was written before is no longer
    # known to be there, and whatever remembers it has to forget it now --
    # the write may land and Home Assistant stop before it returns.
    on_send: Callable[[], None] = lambda: None
    # The lock refused this slot's PIN: the integration turns the slot off and
    # owns the repair that says why.
    on_disable: Callable[[int], None] = lambda slot: None
    # What was last written to a slot before this worker, by an earlier run:
    # a slot starts from it, so a lock that will not show its codes is not
    # written again (#405).
    recall: Callable[[int], str | None] = lambda slot: None
    # The lock answered an earlier run: one not answering now is offline.
    answered_before: bool = False
    slots: dict[int, Slot] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # What the logs call the lock (its entity id).
    name: str = "lock"

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Start idle: nothing queued, the lock never yet reached."""
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[_Job | None] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        # Set when a job is queued: the loop, waiting for a slot's pause or
        # the next probe, takes it at once.
        self._woken = asyncio.Event()
        self._started = False
        self._stopping = False
        self._stopped = asyncio.Event()
        self._queued: set[int] = set()
        # The slot whose sync is running now.
        self._syncing: int | None = None
        self._seq = 0
        self._sent = 0
        self._written: dict[int, int] = {}
        self._last_exchange: float | None = None
        # Exchanges the lock answered: proof it is there.
        self._answers = 0
        # The provider raised something that is not a LockError.
        self._bug = False
        # The lock took a write, and the read-back went unanswered.
        self._lost = False
        # Slots charged a try since the lock last answered, by Slot and epoch:
        # an outage costs each target one try at most.
        self._charged: dict[int, tuple[Slot, int]] = {}
        # Slots written since the lock last gave a reading of them, by the
        # Slot and epoch written for: the write may have landed, so what it
        # said before is no guide to a new target.
        self._unsure: dict[int, tuple[Slot, int]] = {}
        # Slots whose sync failed with nothing answering, by epoch: charged
        # when the lock next answers, as nothing else tells an outage from a
        # slot the lock ignores.
        self._owed: dict[int, tuple[Slot, int]] = {}
        self._probes = 0
        # Slots probed since the lock last answered.
        self._probed: set[int] = set()
        self._no_answers = 0
        self._down_until: float | None = None
        # When the next backoff probe is due, while backing off.
        self._probe_at: float | None = None
        # When each slot's last write was sent, on the monotonic clock: for
        # the logs' timing of pushes, nothing else.
        self._write_sent: dict[int, float] = {}

    # The integration's side -------------------------------------------------

    def want(self, slot: int, pin: Want, *, release: bool = False) -> None:
        """Say what ``slot`` should hold; a release clear when ``release``."""
        if (current := self.slots.get(slot)) is None:
            self.slots[slot] = Slot(pin, wrote=self.recall(slot), release=release)
        else:
            current.aim(pin, release=release)
            if self._unsure_of(slot, current):
                current.doubt(self.salt)
        self.request_sync((slot,), why="want change")

    def forget(self, slot: int) -> None:
        """Stop tracking ``slot`` without touching what the lock holds."""
        self.slots.pop(slot, None)

    def resume(self, slot: int) -> None:
        """Lift ``slot``'s hold: the user acknowledged its repair."""
        if (current := self.slots.get(slot)) is not None:
            current.resume()
            # What polls last read of it may be old: read it before deciding.
            current.seen = None
            self.request_sync((slot,), why="resume")

    def status(self, slot: int) -> tuple[Status, Repair | None]:
        """Return ``slot``'s sync status and the repair it raises, if any."""
        current = self.slots[slot]
        return current.status(self.salt), current.hold

    def wake(self) -> None:
        """
        Probe now if backing off: something says the lock may be back.

        The provider's integration reconnecting, say. Only the probe's
        answer, as always, decides whether the lock is there.
        """
        if self._down_until is None or self._stopping:
            return
        self._down_until = self._probe_at = self.clock()
        self._probe()

    def syncing(self, slot: int) -> bool:
        """Return whether a sync of ``slot`` is queued or running."""
        return slot in self._queued or slot == self._syncing

    @property
    def started(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``start`` was called."""
        return self._started

    @property
    def reachable(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the lock is answering (not backing off)."""
        return self._down_until is None

    @property
    def answered(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the lock has answered this worker at all."""
        return self._answers > 0

    @property
    def answered_ever(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether the lock has answered this worker or an earlier run."""
        return self.answered or self.answered_before

    @property
    def offline(self) -> bool:
        """
        Return whether a lock that answered before has stopped answering.

        A lock that answers for some slots and not others never gets here:
        a slot whose own exchanges go unanswered while another slot answers
        is held instead (#1644). A lock never reached is still coming up, not
        offline (#1257); one that answered an earlier run and is dead at
        this one's start is.
        """
        return self.answered_ever and self._no_answers >= OFFLINE_AFTER

    def request_sync(
        self, slots: Collection[int] | None = None, *, why: str = "request"
    ) -> None:
        """
        Queue a sync of ``slots`` (every tracked one by default), once each.

        Before ``start`` nothing is queued: the first read comes first.
        ``why`` is only for the logs.
        """
        if not self._started:
            return
        for slot in tuple(self.slots if slots is None else slots):
            if slot not in self._queued:
                self._queued.add(slot)
                self._put(_Job("slot", slot=slot), why)

    def push(self, slot: int, reading: Reading) -> None:
        """
        Take what the lock reported on its own about ``slot``.

        A report taken in before the slot's last write finished is dropped
        when its turn comes: the write's read-back is newer.
        """
        sent = self._write_sent.get(slot)
        _LOGGER.debug(
            "%s slot %s: push received, %s ms since last write sent",
            self.name,
            slot,
            "no write" if sent is None else round(_ms(sent)),
        )
        self._put(_Job("push", slot=slot, reading=reading, seq=self._next()), None)

    async def read(
        self, slots: Collection[int] | None = None, *, probe: bool = False
    ) -> dict[int, Reading]:
        """
        Read ``slots`` in the lock's turn: by default every tracked slot.

        A held slot is left out of the read -- a lock that fails a read over
        one slot it ignores would otherwise fail every poll of the rest --
        and one whose hold an agreeing read lifts (``Slot.liftable``) is read
        after it, on its own (``_read_held``). ``probe`` when someone says
        the lock may be back (the hard refresh service): the read goes even
        while backing off, and an answer brings the lock back.
        """
        if self._stopping:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped")
        done: asyncio.Future[Any] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        if slots is None:
            wanted = tuple(n for n, slot in self.slots.items() if slot.hold is None)
            held = tuple(n for n, slot in self.slots.items() if slot.liftable)
        else:
            wanted, held = tuple(slots), ()
        self._put(
            _Job("probe" if probe else "read", slots=wanted, held=held, done=done),
            "caller",
        )
        return await done

    async def turn[T](self, call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
        """
        Run ``call`` against the lock in its turn, as one exchange; return its result.

        For a question about the lock asked through a provider of its own (the
        migration's unmanaged-code sweep): nothing else talks to the lock
        meanwhile, and its answer counts like any other.
        """
        if self._stopping:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped")
        done: asyncio.Future[T] = asyncio.get_running_loop().create_future()
        self._put(_Job("turn", call=call, done=done), "caller")
        return await done

    async def settled(self) -> None:
        """Wait until every job queued so far, and any it queued, is done."""
        await self._queue.join()

    # Lifecycle -----------------------------------------------------------------

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Start the worker: a first read of every tracked slot, then sync."""
        self._started = True
        self._task = asyncio.create_task(self._run(), name="lock worker")
        self._put(_Job("read", slots=tuple(self.slots)), "start")
        # Behind the read, so they find it done -- and still run if it failed.
        self.request_sync(why="start")

    async def stop(self, grace: float = 30.0) -> None:
        """
        Stop for good.

        No new jobs are taken, waiting ones are answered at once, and the job
        running now gets ``grace`` to finish before it is cancelled.
        """
        if self._stopping:
            await self._stopped.wait()
            return
        self._stopping = True
        try:
            self._drain()
            if self._task is not None and not self._task.done():
                self._queue.put_nowait(None)
                self._woken.set()
                try:
                    async with asyncio.timeout(grace):
                        await asyncio.shield(self._task)
                except TimeoutError:
                    self._task.cancel()
                    # A provider that eats the cancel is left behind, not awaited.
                    await asyncio.wait({self._task}, timeout=grace)
        finally:
            # Even if this caller was cancelled: nothing is left running or
            # queued (a cancelled task never reaches the end-of-queue marker),
            # and no later stop() waits for ever.
            if self._task is not None:
                self._task.cancel()
            self._drain()
            self._stopped.set()

    def _drain(self) -> None:
        """Answer and mark done every job still queued."""
        while not self._queue.empty():
            job = self._queue.get_nowait()
            if job is not None:
                _resolve(
                    job.done,
                    error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped"),
                )
            self._queue.task_done()

    def _put(self, job: _Job, why: str | None) -> None:
        """Queue ``job``; log why, unless ``why`` is None (logged already)."""
        if not self._stopping:
            if why is not None:
                _LOGGER.debug(
                    "%s slot %s: queued %s (%s)",
                    self.name,
                    _where(job.slot, job.slots),
                    job.kind,
                    why,
                )
            self._queue.put_nowait(job)
            self._woken.set()

    # The loop ------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _run(self) -> None:
        while True:
            if self._stopping and self._queue.empty():
                return  # it ate stop's cancel; nothing is left to do
            if (job := await self._take()) is None:
                break
            before = self._statuses()
            try:
                await self._do(job)
            except LockError as err:
                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                # Cut off by stop: its caller still gets an answer.
                _resolve(
                    job.done,
                    error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="stopped"),
                )
                raise
            except Exception as err:  # one bad job must not stop the lock
                _LOGGER.exception("Lock job %s failed", job.kind)
                _resolve(job.done, error=err)
            finally:
                self._queue.task_done()
            self._log_transitions(before, job.kind)
            try:
                self.on_change()
            except Exception:  # the integration's trouble must not stop the lock
                _LOGGER.exception("Lock change callback failed")
        self._queue.task_done()

    async def _take(self) -> _Job | None:
        """
        Take the next job, queueing slots and the probe as they fall due.

        The worker owns every timer: with nothing queued, the loop waits for
        the first slot's pause or the next probe to end, or for a job.
        """
        while self._queue.empty() and (deadline := self._deadline()) is not None:
            if (wait := deadline - self.clock()) > 0:
                self._woken.clear()
                timer = asyncio.ensure_future(self.sleep(wait))
                woken = asyncio.ensure_future(self._woken.wait())
                try:
                    await asyncio.wait(
                        (timer, woken), return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED
                    )
                finally:
                    timer.cancel()
                    woken.cancel()
            self._fire()
        return await self._queue.get()

    def _deadline(self) -> float | None:
        """Return when the first slot's pause or the next probe ends, if any."""
        times = [s.not_before for s in self.slots.values() if s.not_before is not None]
        if self._probe_at is not None and self.slots:
            times.append(self._probe_at)
        return min(times, default=None)

    def _fire(self) -> None:
        """Queue each slot whose pause is over, and the probe if it is due."""
        for number, slot in tuple(self.slots.items()):
            if slot.not_before is not None and not self._paused(slot):
                self.request_sync((number,), why="retry")
        if self._probe_at is not None and self._probe_at <= self.clock():
            self._probe()

    def _paused(self, slot: Slot) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``slot`` is waiting out a pause; forget one that is over."""
        if slot.not_before is not None and slot.not_before <= self.clock():
            slot.not_before = None
        return slot.not_before is not None

    def _statuses(self) -> dict[int, Status] | None:
        """Return each slot's status, for logging its changes; None if not logged."""
        if not _LOGGER.isEnabledFor(logging.DEBUG):
            return None
        return {number: slot.status(self.salt) for number, slot in self.slots.items()}

    def _log_transitions(self, before: dict[int, Status] | None, kind: str) -> None:
        """Log each slot whose status a job changed."""
        if before is None:
            return
        for number, slot in self.slots.items():
            if (was := before.get(number)) is not (now := slot.status(self.salt)):
                _LOGGER.debug(
                    "%s slot %s: status %s -> %s (after %s)",
                    self.name,
                    number,
                    was,
                    now,
                    kind,
                )

    async def _do(self, job: _Job) -> None:
        if job.kind == "push":
            self._take_push(job)
            return
        if job.kind == "slot":
            assert job.slot is not None
            self._queued.discard(job.slot)
        if self._down_until is not None and job.kind != "probe":
            # Backing off: callers hear at once that the lock is not
            # answering; slot syncs are queued again once it answers.
            _resolve(job.done, error=LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False))
            return
        if job.kind == "slot":
            assert job.slot is not None
            self._syncing = job.slot
            try:
                await self._sync(job.slot)
            finally:
                self._syncing = None
            self._again(job.slot)
            return
        if job.kind == "turn":
            assert job.call is not None
            _resolve(job.done, await self._exchange(job.call, op="turn"))
            return
        # A probe left unanswered schedules the next one through _no_answer.
        readings = await self._read(job.slots, op=job.kind)
        for number in job.held:
            readings.update(await self._read_held(number))
        _resolve(job.done, readings)

    async def _read_held(self, number: int) -> dict[int, Reading]:
        """
        Read a slot held after its tries on its own: an agreeing reading lifts it.

        Nothing is written or charged for it whatever it says, and its
        failure is nobody's: a slot the lock ignores, held for that, never
        backs the lock off or fails the read of the rest.
        """
        try:
            return await self._read((number,), op="held read", count=False)
        except LockError:
            return {}

    def _take_push(self, job: _Job) -> None:
        assert job.slot is not None and job.reading is not None
        slot = self.slots.get(job.slot)
        if slot is None or self._written.get(job.slot, 0) > job.seq:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s slot %s: push dropped (untracked, or older than the last write)",
                self.name,
                job.slot,
            )
            return
        if self._unsure_of(job.slot, slot):
            # A report may be a cache older than that write: it is no fight,
            # and no reason to stop trusting what was written.
            slot.seen = job.reading
            slot.doubt(self.salt)
        else:
            slot.observe(job.reading, self.salt, self.clock(), fresh=False)
        self.request_sync((job.slot,), why="push")

    def _unsure_of(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> bool:
        """Return whether a write for another target may have landed since a reading."""
        unsure = self._unsure.get(number)
        return unsure is not None and (unsure[0] is not slot or unsure[1] != slot.epoch)

    async def _sync(self, number: int) -> None:
        """
        Bring one slot in line: read it if never read, write it if it differs.

        A sync that ends out of sync costs the slot one try, charged once the
        lock has shown it is there: at once if anything in the sync was
        answered, else when the lock next answers. Between two answers a slot
        is charged once at most, so an outage costs it one try at most. A
        provider bug is the slot's: charged at once, every time. Nothing is
        awaited between looking and charging, and a sync begun before the
        counts started over is not charged.

        So every sync that does not end in sync is charged, or owed while
        nothing answers -- and only an answer resets the lock's no-answers:
        each slot ends in sync, held, or with the lock offline.
        """
        if (slot := self.slots.get(number)) is None:
            return
        epoch, answers, self._bug = slot.epoch, self._answers, False
        # Waiting out a pause: a read still goes, but nothing is written or
        # charged before the pause ends -- whatever queued this sync.
        paused = self._paused(slot)
        try:
            if slot.status(self.salt) is Status.UNKNOWN:
                await self._read((number,), follow=False, op="first read")
            if slot.status(self.salt) is Status.OUT_OF_SYNC and not paused:
                await self._write(number, slot)
        except LockError as err:
            _LOGGER.debug("Sync of slot %s failed: %s", number, err)
            if err.kind is ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED and slot.epoch == epoch:
                # A read refused for the slot (past the lock's capacity).
                slot.refused(value=False, why=err.message)
        if slot.epoch == epoch and not paused and self._failed(slot):
            if self._bug:
                slot.tried()
            elif self._answers > answers and not self._lost:
                self._charge(number, slot)
            elif not self._was_charged(number, slot):
                self._owed[number] = (slot, epoch)
        # A read-back lost in this sync is settled: owed, or nothing to owe.
        self._lost = False
        if (
            slot.release
            and slot.status(self.salt) is Status.IN_SYNC
            and self.slots.get(number) is slot
        ):
            del self.slots[number]

    def _failed(self, slot: Slot) -> bool:
        return slot.status(self.salt) in (Status.UNKNOWN, Status.OUT_OF_SYNC)

    def _charge(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> None:
        """Charge ``slot`` one try, unless charged since the lock last answered."""
        if not self._was_charged(number, slot):
            self._charged[number] = (slot, slot.epoch)
            slot.tried()

    def _was_charged(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> bool:
        """Return whether this target was charged since the lock last answered."""
        charged = self._charged.get(number)
        return charged is not None and charged[0] is slot and charged[1] == slot.epoch

    async def _write(self, number: int, slot: Slot) -> None:
        """
        Write what is wanted, then read it back.

        What was sent is what is recorded; if the slot changed hands or wants
        another PIN by the time the write is back, nothing is recorded or read
        back; the write may have landed, so ``want`` doubted what the lock
        last said (``Slot.doubt``). A refusal holds at once.
        Anything else, even a write that never left, is read back -- unless
        the lock has just gone into backoff -- and a cause the provider named
        is kept, so a slot held after its tries says it.

        A read-back left unanswered after a write the lock took is owed, not
        charged: the slot is read afresh next, and only that answer says
        whether the write failed (#1397). Silence is never an answer: it
        still counts toward the lock backing off.
        """
        pin = slot.want
        slot.wrote = None
        took = False

        def current() -> bool:
            # Still the slot in place, still wanting what was sent.
            return self.slots.get(number) is slot and slot.want == pin

        op = "clear" if pin is None else "set"
        # Forgotten or retargeted while waiting its turn: send nothing.
        await self._pace(op, number)
        if not current():
            return
        self._unsure[number] = (slot, slot.epoch)
        try:
            self.on_send()
        except Exception:  # the integration's trouble must not stop the lock
            _LOGGER.exception("Lock send callback failed")
        try:
            # Reports taken in before the write is sent are older than it.
            changed = await self._exchange(
                lambda: self.port.write(number, pin), mark=number, op=op
            )
        except LockError as err:
            if not current():
                return
            # If it is held after its tries, a cause the provider named says why.
            slot.cause = err.cause
            if err.kind is ErrorKind.ALREADY_SO:
                slot.wrote_want(self.salt)
                slot.released = slot.release
                took = True
            elif err.kind is ErrorKind.VALUE_REFUSED:
                slot.refused(value=True, why=err.message)
                if pin is not None:
                    self.on_disable(number)
                return
            elif err.kind is ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED:
                slot.refused(value=False, why=err.message)
                return
        else:
            if not current():
                return
            slot.cause = ""
            slot.released = slot.release
            if changed is not False:
                slot.wrote_want(self.salt)
            took = True
        if self._down_until is None:
            missed = self._no_answers
            try:
                await self._read((number,), follow=False, op="read-back")
            except LockError:
                if took and self._no_answers > missed:
                    slot.seen = None
                    self._lost = True
                raise

    def _next(self) -> int:
        """Return the next point in the order reports and exchanges happen."""
        self._seq += 1
        return self._seq

    async def _read(
        self,
        numbers: Collection[int],
        *,
        follow: bool = True,
        op: str = "read",
        count: bool = True,
    ) -> dict[int, Reading]:
        """
        Read ``numbers``; unless ``follow`` is off, queue any slot that needs work.

        A slot whose hold the reading lifted is synced again: nothing to
        write, but a release in sync is done. ``count`` off: no answer is not
        counted against the lock.

        A reading is newer than every report on its slot taken in before the
        read was sent; one taken in while it was out may be newer, and is
        kept. A slot the read left out says nothing, and drops no report.
        """
        if not numbers:
            # Reading nothing asks the lock nothing: no answer, no no-answer.
            return {}

        until the lock next answers -- and with no answer, the lock backs off
        on its way to the offline repair. So this ends in sync, held, or with
        the lock offline -- never in a loop. (A job queued while backing off
        fails at once, and an answer queues every slot again.)

        taken in before then are dropped.

        No answer -- the budget running out, a ``NO_ANSWER``, a transient
        failure that never left for the lock, or a network error -- counts
        against the lock. Any other ``LockError`` that was sent is the lock
        answering, refusals included. One that never left (the integration
        refusing) and anything else a provider raises (a bug in it, logged)

        the slot it hits -- or, on a probe, no answer, so probing goes on.

                    op,
                    wait * 1000,

        self._down_until = None

            self._probe_at = None

        """Take the owed tries: the lock answered, so they were the slots'."""
        owed, self._owed = self._owed, {}

            (number, owing)
            for number, (owing, epoch) in owed.items()
            if owing.epoch == epoch and self._failed(owing)
        ]

        for number, slot in self._due() if due is None else due:

    A refusal is the lock's answer about the slot. Any other failure is no
    answer: providers wrap an integration or cloud outage as a failed
    operation, and a slot is still charged when the lock answers anything
    else in its sync, such as the read-back.

    if isinstance(err, CodeRejectedError):
        # A refused clear holds at once; a refused PIN turns the slot off.
        kind = ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED if clearing else ErrorKind.VALUE_REFUSED
    elif isinstance(err, LockOperationUnsupported):
        kind = ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED
    elif isinstance(err, (LockOperationError, LockBusy)):
        kind = ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER
    else:
        return None
    cause = str(err) if isinstance(err, LockOperationBlocked) else ""
    return LockError(kind, message=str(err), cause=cause)


class ProviderPort:
    """``LockPort`` for an existing provider, and its stand-in coordinator."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        provider: BaseLock,
        name_for: Callable[[int], str | None] = lambda slot: None,
        polling: Callable[[], bool] = lambda: True,
        reports: dict[str, bool] | None = None,
        on_reports: Callable[[], None] = lambda: None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Wrap ``provider``.

        ``name_for`` names the user a slot's PIN is written for; ``polling``
        says whether the lock is polled ("Disable polling" spares the drift
        check). ``reports`` is shared by every port for the run: lock's
        entity registry id -> whether a read of it has described a slot (see
        ``read``), so a device re-paired under the same entity id starts over;
        ``on_reports`` is called when a read of this lock first does.
        """
        self.provider = provider
        self.name_for = name_for
        self.polling = polling
        # The worker that owns the lock: set once it is built.
        self.worker: LockWorker[ProviderPort] | None = None
        # The slot a write is in the provider for: its own echo is not the lock.
        self._writing: int | None = None
        # When each slot was last written, on the event loop's clock: a
        # provider whose reads lag its writes reads it as silent until then.
        self._written_at: dict[int, float] = {}
        # Slots given up: clearing one releases it -- nothing untagged is
        # adopted, and a native-user provider deletes the user it tagged.
        self.releasing: set[int] = set()
        # Of those, the ones the store showed a PIN Lock Code Manager wrote
        # when the release began: the release's own send forgets it.
        self._written: set[int] = set()
        # What the lock last said of any slot, by read or by push: codes
        # nobody here manages, and the last word on a slot the worker has let
        # go. The worker's own view of a slot it tracks comes first.
        self.others: dict[int, Reading] = {}
        # Some read has said something about a slot: silence is now no answer.
        self._answered = False
        # Every lock read this run, by registry id -> whether a read described
        # a slot of it. Kept past this port: a one-off read builds a port per
        # read.
        self.reports: dict[str, bool] = {} if reports is None else reports
        self.on_reports = on_reports
        # Slots the lock last answered it cannot tell what they hold.
        self.not_reported: set[int] = set()
        self._poll: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._poll_unsubs: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
        # Unloaded: nothing may start a poll or arm its timer again.
        self._closed = False
        # This port set the provider up, and owns its lifecycle.
        self._managed = False
        # Its setup raised what no provider handler expects: nothing retries
        # that short of a reload, so nothing can be sent to the lock.
        self.setup_crashed = False
        self._unsubs: list[Callable[[], None]] = []

    @property
    def managed(self) -> bool:
        """Return whether this port set the provider up and owns its lifecycle."""
        return self._managed

    # LockPort ----------------------------------------------------------------

    async def _timed[T](
        self, op: str, slots: Any, call: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]
    ) -> T:
        """Run one provider call, logging its start and how long it took."""
        entity_id = self.provider.lock.entity_id
        _LOGGER.debug("%s slot %s: provider %s start", entity_id, slots, op)
        start = time.monotonic()
        outcome = "ok"
        try:
            return await call()
        except BaseException as err:
            kind = getattr(err, "kind", None)
            outcome = kind.value if isinstance(kind, ErrorKind) else type(err).__name__
            raise
        finally:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s slot %s: provider %s %s in %.0f ms",
                entity_id,
                slots,
                op,
                outcome,
                (time.monotonic() - start) * 1000,
            )

    async def read(self, slots: Collection[int]) -> dict[int, Reading]:
        """Ask the lock about ``slots`` now (see ``_read``), timed for the logs."""
        op = (
            "read (hard refresh)"
            if self.provider.fresh_read_is_hard_refresh
            else "read (get usercodes)"
        )
        where = tuple(slots)
        return await self._timed(
            op, where[0] if len(where) == 1 else where, lambda: self._read(slots)
        )

    async def _read(self, slots: Collection[int]) -> dict[int, Reading]:
        """
        Ask the lock about ``slots`` now.

        Bounded by the provider's own budget for a walk of that many slots.
        A slot the lock said nothing about is left out (silent); a read where
        it said nothing about any of them, from a lock that has answered
        reads before, is no answer -- unless, of some, it answered that it
        cannot tell.

        A slot it answered it cannot tell of is silent too (#1581), unless a
        read has described some slot of the lock this run: a lock that can
        report its codes and will not report this one holds a code there.
        """
        provider = self.provider
        if self._managed and not await self._set_up():
            raise LockError(
                ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="provider not set up"
            )
        await self._available()
        fetch = (
            provider.async_hard_refresh_codes
            if provider.fresh_read_is_hard_refresh
            else provider.async_get_usercodes
        )
        provider.last_silent_slots = provider.last_foreign_slots = frozenset()
        provider.last_cannot_tell_slots = frozenset()
        # A slot past the lock's capacity is never asked about: no answer
        # would come, and the lock would be taken for gone (#1398). Its write
        # is refused unsent, which holds it.
        slots = [slot for slot in slots if await self._within_capacity(slot)]
        if not slots:
            # Nothing was asked: not the lock answering, or a probe of a slot
            # past capacity would end an outage's backoff.
            raise LockError(
                ErrorKind.SLOT_REFUSED, sent=False, message="past the lock's capacity"
            )
        try:
            async with asyncio.timeout(provider._operation_budget(len(slots))):
                codes = await fetch(slots)
        except TimeoutError as err:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, message="read timed out") from err
        except LockCodeManagerProviderError as err:
            if lock_error(err, clearing=False) is None:
                raise
            # A read that failed said nothing about any slot: no answer.
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, message=str(err)) from err
        silent = provider.last_silent_slots & set(slots)
        cannot_tell = provider.last_cannot_tell_slots & silent
        if self._answered and silent >= set(slots) and not cannot_tell:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, message="the lock said nothing")
        lock = provider.lock.id
        # Any slot asked about and not silent was described, named in the
        # answer or not: a provider projecting only the slots an entry manages
        # (Z-Wave JS's hard refresh) leaves an empty one it was asked about
        # out, and that is no lock that cannot report.
        if not self.reports.get(lock) and set(slots) - silent:
            self.reports[lock] = True
            self.on_reports()
        if self.reports.setdefault(lock, False):
            silent -= cannot_tell
        self.not_reported.difference_update(slots)
        self.not_reported |= cannot_tell
        # The lock answered, but of a slot written too lately to show it yet:
        # left out (silent), so the write is trusted until a later read.
        silent |= self._lagging(slots)
        # Someone else's code at a slot's index is not the slot's: a slot
        # turned off is clear, and one wanting a PIN writes it, which adopts
        # the user (#1695). It is still a code nobody here manages.
        foreign = provider.last_foreign_slots
        readings = {
            slot: Seen.EMPTY if slot in foreign else reading(codes[slot])
            for slot in slots
            if slot in codes and slot not in silent
        }
        heard = {
            slot: reading(credential)
            for slot, credential in codes.items()
            if slot not in silent
        }
        if provider.per_exchange_budget is None:
            # A provider that reads the whole lock in one call tells of every
            # code on it: one it no longer tells of is gone (deleted at the
            # keypad, say). What it said nothing about stays as it was.
            self.others = {
                **{slot: seen for slot, seen in self.others.items() if slot in silent},
                **heard,
            }
        else:
            # One that walks the slots asked for says nothing of the rest.
            self.others.update(heard)
        self._answered = self._answered or bool(readings)
        return readings

    def _duplicate_of(self, slot: int, pin: str) -> int | None:
        """
        Return another slot ``pin`` is on, or is wanted on; None if none.

        A tracked slot counts by what it wants (one on its way to another
        PIN, or out, does not); any other slot by what the lock said of it.
        """
        tracked = {} if self.worker is None else self.worker.slots
        for other, held in self.others.items():
            if other != slot and other not in tracked and held == Holds(pin):
                return other
        return next(
            (
                other
                for other, current in tracked.items()
                if other != slot and current.want == pin and not current.release
            ),
            None,
        )

    def release(self, slot: int, *, written: bool) -> None:
        """
        Make ``slot``'s next clear a release.

        ``written``: the store shows a PIN Lock Code Manager wrote there.
        Taken now: the worker forgets what it wrote as it sends the clear.
        """
        self.releasing.add(slot)
        if written:
            self._written.add(slot)
        else:
            self._written.discard(slot)

    async def write(self, slot: int, pin: str | None) -> bool | None:
        """Put ``pin`` in ``slot``, or clear it (see ``_write``), timed for the logs."""
        op = "clear" if pin is None else "set"
        return await self._timed(op, slot, lambda: self._write(slot, pin))

    async def _write(self, slot: int, pin: str | None) -> bool | None:
        """
        Put ``pin`` in ``slot``, or clear it for None.

        Nothing is sent before the provider is set up, or for a slot past
        the lock's capacity (#1398).
        """
        provider = self.provider
        if not await self._set_up():
            raise LockError(
                ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message="provider not set up"
            )
        await self._available()
        self._writing = slot
        if pin is None:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Clearing usercode on %s slot %s (source=%s)",
                provider.lock.entity_id,
                slot,
                "sync",

        else:

            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Setting usercode on %s slot %s (pin=%s, source=%s)",
                provider.lock.entity_id,
                slot,
                provider.mask_pin(pin, slot),
                "sync",

                await provider.async_release_managed_slot(
                    slot, written=slot in self._written

                return await provider.async_clear_usercode(slot)

                await self._capacity(slot)
                if (other := self._duplicate_of(slot, pin)) is not None:

                    # as the other, and turning one off leaves it working.

                        code_slot=slot,

        Asking is what retries a deferred setup; a provider with no
        connection check (Z-Wave JS) is asked nowhere else. Reads are gated
        too once this port set the provider up: a lock that answers reads
        while every write is refused unsent would charge each slot's sync
        (the read-back answers) and hold it. A provider this port never set
        up (a one-off read's) is only read.

        if not provider.provider_setup_succeeded:

        except LockCodeManagerError as err:
            raise LockError(ErrorKind.NO_ANSWER, sent=False, message=str(err)) from err

    # Lifecycle ---------------------------------------------------------------

    async def async_setup(self, config_entry: ConfigEntry) -> None:
        """Set the provider up with the stand-in coordinator; start the cadence."""
        provider = self.provider
        self._managed = True
        try:
            await provider.async_setup_internal(config_entry, _Coordinator(self))
        except Exception:
            self.setup_crashed = True
            raise

            # connection check is what retries a deferred setup.
            self._arm_poll()

                    async_track_time_interval(
                        provider.hass,
                        self._check_connection,
                        interval,
                        cancel_on_shutdown=True,

    async def async_unload(self, remove_permanently: bool) -> None:
        """Stop the cadence and unload the provider."""
        self._closed = True
        for unsub in self._unsubs:
            unsub()
        self._unsubs.clear()
        for unsub in self._poll_unsubs:
            unsub()
        self._poll_unsubs.clear()
        if self._poll is not None:
            self._poll.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(self._poll, return_exceptions=True)

    # What the provider pushes and asks for -------------------------------------

    def pushed(self, slot: int, credential: SlotCredential) -> None:
        """Hand the worker what the lock reported on its own about ``slot``."""
        if self.worker is None or slot == self._writing:
            # A provider echoing the write it is making is not the lock.
            return
        self.not_reported.discard(slot)
        if slot not in self.worker.slots:
            self.others[slot] = reading(credential)
            return
        self.worker.push(slot, reading(credential))

    def poll(self) -> None:
        """Read every slot the worker tracks, unless a poll is still out."""
        if self.worker is None or not self.worker.started:
            return
        if self._poll is None or self._poll.done():
            self._poll = self.provider.hass.async_create_background_task(
                self._read_tracked(), f"Poll {self.provider.lock.entity_id}"
            )

    def wants_pin(self, slot: int) -> bool:
        """Return whether ``slot`` should hold a PIN."""
        current = None if self.worker is None else self.worker.slots.get(slot)
        return current is not None and current.want is not None

    async def _read_tracked(self) -> None:
        assert self.worker is not None
        try:
            await self.worker.read()
        except LockError as err:
            # The worker has counted it; nothing else to do.
            _LOGGER.debug("Poll of %s failed: %s", self.provider.lock.entity_id, err)

    def _cadence(self) -> tuple[timedelta | None, timedelta | None]:
        """
        Return the scan interval (a lock that does not push) and the drift check's.

        Every read is fresh, so both are plain reads; only the scan gives way
        to "Disable polling".

        provider = self.provider
        scan = None if provider.supports_push else provider.usercode_scan_interval

        for unsub in self._poll_unsubs:
            unsub()
        self._poll_unsubs.clear()

            return
        scan, drift = self._cadence()
        for interval, action in ((scan, self._on_scan), (drift, self._on_poll)):
            if interval:
                self._poll_unsubs.append(
                    async_track_time_interval(
                        self.provider.hass, action, interval, cancel_on_shutdown=True
                    )
                )

    @callback
    def _on_scan(self, now: datetime) -> None:
        if self.polling():

    @callback
    def _on_poll(self, now: datetime) -> None:
        self.poll()

    async def _check_connection(self, now: datetime) -> None:
        """Let the provider see its integration come and go, to resubscribe."""
        try:
            await self.provider.async_internal_is_reachable()
        except LockCodeManagerError as err:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "Connection check failed for %s: %s",
                self.provider.lock.entity_id,
                err,
            )

"""
What the lock workers remember across a restart, in one Home Assistant Store.

Per lock, keyed by the entity registry id its worker is bound to, so a rename
keeps it (#1442) and a device re-paired under the same entity id never finds
the old one's, with its entity id beside it: whether the lock has ever
answered, whether a read of it has ever described a slot (#1581; absent in a
record saved before, and then not known to), and per slot what was last
written -- a keyed fingerprint or ``cleared``, never a PIN -- and a release
clear still owed, with the entry that gave the slot up. What a slot holds is
read again; counts, fights and holds start over (a hold's repair outlives a
restart on its own).

Written a second after a change, and at Home Assistant's final write. Never
dropped on an unload (#1243): only when a release is done, a slot is let go
of for good, a lock leaves Lock Code Manager or an entry is deleted. A
record whose registry id is gone goes at the next start.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable, Collection
from typing import Any

from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, callback
from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er
from homeassistant.helpers.storage import Store

from ..const import DOMAIN
from ..sync.slot import CLEARED
from ..sync.worker import LockWorker

STORE_KEY = f"{DOMAIN}.core"
STORE_VERSION = 1
SAVE_DELAY = 1.0

Record = dict[str, Any]


class LockStore:
    """Each lock's record, under ``key``: the registry id its worker is bound to."""

    def __init__(self, hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
        """Start empty; ``async_load`` reads what was saved."""
        self._hass = hass
        self._store: Store[dict[str, Any]] = Store(hass, STORE_VERSION, STORE_KEY)
        self._locks: dict[str, Record] = {}

    async def async_load(self) -> None:
        """Read what was saved, each record under its lock's current entity id."""
        saved = await self._store.async_load() or {}
        self._locks = saved.get("locks", {})
        registry = er.async_get(self._hass)
        for key, record in self._locks.items():
            if (entity := registry.async_get(key)) is not None:
                record["entity_id"] = entity.entity_id

    # What a lock's worker starts from ------------------------------------------

    def wrote(self, key: str, slot: int) -> str | None:
        """Return what was last written to ``slot`` on the lock, if anything."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)
        return (
            None if record is None else record["slots"].get(str(slot), {}).get("wrote")
        )

    def wrote_pin(self, key: str, slot: int) -> bool:
        """
        Return whether a PIN was what was last written to ``slot`` on the lock.

        A slot only ever cleared never held Lock Code Manager's code.
        """
        return self.wrote(key, slot) not in (None, CLEARED)

    def answered(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether the lock has ever answered."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)
        return record is not None and record["answered"]

    def reports(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether a read of the lock has ever described a slot."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)
        return record is not None and record.get("reports", False)

    def releases(self) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
        """Return each release clear still owed: lock, slot, the entry that gave it up."""
        return [
            (record["entity_id"], int(slot), saved["release"])
            for record in self._locks.values()
            for slot, saved in record["slots"].items()
            if "release" in saved
        ]

    # Keeping it current --------------------------------------------------------

    @callback
    def remember(
        self,
        key: str,
        lock: str,
        worker: LockWorker,
        given_up_by: Callable[[int], str | None],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Take what ``worker`` knows of ``lock`` now; slots it no longer tracks keep theirs.

        A release is kept while it is still going, not once held: its repair
        brings it back. ``given_up_by`` names the entry that gave a slot up.
        """
        record = self._locks.get(key, {"answered": False, "slots": {}})
        slots = dict(record["slots"])
        for number, slot in worker.slots.items():
            saved: dict[str, str] = {}
            if slot.wrote is not None:
                saved["wrote"] = slot.wrote
            if slot.release and slot.hold is None and (by := given_up_by(number)):
                saved["release"] = by
            if saved:
                slots[str(number)] = saved
            else:
                slots.pop(str(number), None)
        self._put(
            key,
            {
                **record,
                "entity_id": lock,
                "answered": worker.answered_ever,
                "slots": slots,
            },
        )

    @callback
    def reported(self, key: str, lock: str) -> None:
        """Remember that a read of ``lock`` has described a slot."""
        record = self._locks.get(key, {"answered": False, "slots": {}})
        self._put(key, {**record, "entity_id": lock, "reports": True})

    @callback
    def unreported(self, key: str) -> None:
        """Forget that a read of the lock has described a slot: it is asked again."""
        if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
            self._put(key, {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != "reports"})

    @callback
    def forget_slot(self, key: str, slot: int) -> None:
        """Forget ``slot`` on the lock: it is done, or let go of for good."""
        if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
            slots = {n: s for n, s in record["slots"].items() if n != str(slot)}
            self._put(key, {**record, "slots": slots})

    @callback
    def forget_lock(self, key: str) -> None:
        """Forget the lock: it left Lock Code Manager, or its device is gone."""
        if self._locks.pop(key, None) is not None:
            self._save()

    @callback
    def forget_entry(self, keys: Collection[str], slots: Collection[int]) -> None:
        """
        Forget a deleted entry's ``slots`` on the locks kept under ``keys``.

        A clear it left going is on a slot it no longer has: it is kept.
        """
        for key in keys:
            if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
                kept = {n: s for n, s in record["slots"].items() if int(n) not in slots}
                self._put(key, {**record, "slots": kept})

    @callback
    def prune(self, keep: Collection[str]) -> list[Record]:
        """
        Forget every lock not in ``keep``, or gone; return the records forgotten.

        A record kept under a registry id the registry no longer has was for
        a lock that is gone, even if another now has its entity id.
        """
        registry = er.async_get(self._hass)
        kept = {
            k: r
            for k, r in self._locks.items()
            if r["entity_id"] in keep and registry.async_get(k) is not None
        }
        dropped = [r for k, r in self._locks.items() if k not in kept]
        if dropped:
            self._locks = kept
            self._save()
        return dropped

    # Inside --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _put(self, key: str, record: Record) -> None:
        if self._locks.get(key) != record:
            self._locks[key] = record
            self._save()

    def _save(self) -> None:
        self._store.async_delay_save(lambda: {"locks": self._locks}, SAVE_DELAY)

        """Return what was last written to ``slot`` on the lock, if anything."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)

            None if record is None else record["slots"].get(str(slot), {}).get("wrote")
        )

        """

        A slot only ever cleared never held Lock Code Manager's code.
        """
        return self.wrote(key, slot) not in (None, CLEARED)

    def answered(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether the lock has ever answered."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)
        return record is not None and record["answered"]

    def reports(self, key: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether a read of the lock has ever described a slot."""
        record = self._locks.get(key)
        return record is not None and record.get("reports", False)

    def releases(self) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
        """Return each release clear still owed: lock, slot, the entry that gave it up."""
        return [
            (record["entity_id"], int(slot), saved["release"])
            for record in self._locks.values()
            for slot, saved in record["slots"].items()
            if "release" in saved

    @callback
    def remember(
        self,
        key: str,
        lock: str,
        worker: LockWorker,
        given_up_by: Callable[[int], str | None],
    ) -> None:

        A release is kept while it is still going, not once held: its repair
        brings it back. ``given_up_by`` names the entry that gave a slot up.
        """
        record = self._locks.get(key, {"answered": False, "slots": {}})
        slots = dict(record["slots"])
        for number, slot in worker.slots.items():
            saved: dict[str, str] = {}
            if slot.wrote is not None:
                saved["wrote"] = slot.wrote
            if slot.release and slot.hold is None and (by := given_up_by(number)):
                saved["release"] = by
            if saved:
                slots[str(number)] = saved
            else:
                slots.pop(str(number), None)

            key,
            {
                **record,
                "entity_id": lock,
                "answered": worker.answered_ever,
                "slots": slots,
            },
        )

    def reported(self, key: str, lock: str) -> None:
        """Remember that a read of ``lock`` has described a slot."""
        record = self._locks.get(key, {"answered": False, "slots": {}})
        self._put(key, {**record, "entity_id": lock, "reports": True})

    @callback
    def unreported(self, key: str) -> None:
        """Forget that a read of the lock has described a slot: it is asked again."""
        if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
            self._put(key, {k: v for k, v in record.items() if k != "reports"})

    @callback
    def forget_slot(self, key: str, slot: int) -> None:
        """Forget ``slot`` on the lock: it is done, or let go of for good."""
        if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
            slots = {n: s for n, s in record["slots"].items() if n != str(slot)}
            self._put(key, {**record, "slots": slots})

    @callback
    def forget_lock(self, key: str) -> None:
        """Forget the lock: it left Lock Code Manager, or its device is gone."""
        if self._locks.pop(key, None) is not None:
            self._save()

    @callback
    def forget_entry(self, keys: Collection[str], slots: Collection[int]) -> None:
        """
        Forget a deleted entry's ``slots`` on the locks kept under ``keys``.

        A clear it left going is on a slot it no longer has: it is kept.
        """
        for key in keys:
            if (record := self._locks.get(key)) is not None:
                kept = {n: s for n, s in record["slots"].items() if int(n) not in slots}
                self._put(key, {**record, "slots": kept})

    @callback
    def prune(self, keep: Collection[str]) -> list[Record]:
        """
        Forget every lock not in ``keep``, or gone; return the records forgotten.

        A record kept under a registry id the registry no longer has was for
        a lock that is gone, even if another now has its entity id.
        """
        registry = er.async_get(self._hass)
        kept = {
            k: r
            for k, r in self._locks.items()
            if r["entity_id"] in keep and registry.async_get(k) is not None
        }
        dropped = [r for k, r in self._locks.items() if k not in kept]
        if dropped:
            self._locks = kept
            self._save()
        return dropped

    # Inside --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _put(self, key: str, record: Record) -> None:
        if self._locks.get(key) != record:
            self._locks[key] = record
            self._save()

    def _save(self) -> None:
        self._store.async_delay_save(lambda: {"locks": self._locks}, SAVE_DELAY)

    under the same friendly name) has a new registry id. The worker's
    provider is bound to the old one, so the lock looks offline until the
    entries holding it set up again. Checked at each registry event for the
    lock, and when an entry takes a lock still on its old device, except
    while a check or rebuild of it is under way. A removal alone, or a
    rename (the same registry id), is no rebuild; a removal followed by a
    creation is one, once the creation is in.
    """

    @callback
    def _changed(event: Event[er.EventEntityRegistryUpdatedData]) -> None:
        if (lock := event.data["entity_id"]) in entry.runtime_data.locks:

def _async_check_re_pair(hass: HomeAssistant, lock: str) -> None:
    """
    Check ``lock`` for a re-pair, and rebuild it, unless a check is under way.

    In a task of its own, run once its caller is done: an entry that has
    just taken the lock holds it by then.
    """
    data = hass.data[DATA]
    pending = data[REBUILDS_KEY]
    if lock in pending:
        return
    pending.add(lock)

    async def _check() -> None:
        try:
            # Checked once the rebuild before it is done: it may have rebuilt
            # this lock too.
            async with data[REBUILD_LOCK_KEY]:
                await _async_rebuild_if_re_paired(hass, lock)

            pending.discard(lock)

    hass: HomeAssistant, lock: str, worker: LockWorker[ProviderPort]

    """
    Return whether ``lock``'s entity id names a device other than ``worker``'s.

    A device re-paired under the same entity id has a new registry id: the
    worker, bound to the old one, drives a device that is gone. A lock
    removed, or renamed (the same registry id), is not re-paired.
    """
    entity = er.async_get(hass).async_get(lock)
    return entity is not None and entity.id != worker.port.provider.lock.id


async def _async_rebuild_if_re_paired(hass: HomeAssistant, lock: str) -> None:
    """
    Start ``lock``'s worker over if its entity id now names another device.

    The entries holding it unload together, as a reload would, so its last
    holder stops the worker; they set up again, building a new provider and
    worker with every slot they want. The old worker stops as a lock leaving
    Lock Code Manager does (``_re_paired``). Clears owed to the old device
    are moot: it is gone; a repair names their slots, which the same lock
    re-paired may still hold.
    """
    data = hass.data[DATA]
    registry = lock_registry(hass)
    if (worker := registry.worker(lock)) is None or not _re_paired(hass, lock, worker):
        return  # not running, removed, or the same device (perhaps renamed)
    holders = [
        entry
        for entry in iter_loaded_lcm_entries(hass)
        if lock in entry.runtime_data.locks
    ]
    if not holders:
        return
    _LOGGER.info("%s is a different device now (re-paired): starting it over", lock)
    moot = sorted(n for n, slot in worker.slots.items() if slot.release)
    _async_report_dropped_work(hass, lock, moot)
    for slot in moot:
        worker.forget(slot)
        data[GIVEN_UP_KEY].pop((lock, slot), None)
    unloaded = await asyncio.gather(
        *(hass.config_entries.async_unload(entry.entry_id) for entry in holders),
        return_exceptions=True,
    )
    for entry, result in zip(holders, unloaded, strict=True):
        if isinstance(result, BaseException):
            _LOGGER.error(
                "Unloading %s for re-paired %s failed: %s", entry.title, lock, result

"""

the package. ``model/`` is shared by providers and the HA layer, so it never
imports either. Providers never import the HA layer. Every import counts,
including those under ``TYPE_CHECKING`` and inside functions: a layer that
names another only for typing still depends on it.
"""

import ast
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

PACKAGE = "custom_components.lock_code_manager"
PACKAGE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent.parent / "custom_components" / "lock_code_manager"


def _module_name(path: Path) -> str:
    """Return the dotted module name of a file in the package."""
    parts = path.relative_to(PACKAGE_DIR.parent.parent).with_suffix("").parts
    if parts[-1] == "__init__":
        parts = parts[:-1]
    return ".".join(parts)


def _imports(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """
    Return every module ``path`` imports, as absolute dotted names.

    ``from X import name`` yields both ``X`` and ``X.name``, because ``name``
    may be a submodule (``from ..ha import runtime``).
    """
    module = _module_name(path)
    package = module if path.name == "__init__.py" else module.rpartition(".")[0]
    found: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(ast.parse(path.read_text(), filename=str(path))):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            found.update(alias.name for alias in node.names)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            if node.level:
                base = package.split(".")
                base = base[: len(base) - (node.level - 1)]
                source = ".".join([*base, node.module] if node.module else base)
            else:
                source = node.module or ""
            found.add(source)

    return [

content.thinking:
Since sync can't import the model, I'm thinking the worker needs to be generic over a key type that's hashable and orderable, keeping sync pure while the HA layer instantiates it with the concrete provider port and credential address types. The tricky part is that the registry still needs per-slot ownership tracking tied to that generic key.

Ownership really has to be per-slot rather than per-address, since two entries sharing user slot 3 on a lock would conflict even if they claim different credential kinds (password vs pin) — so a registry keyed purely by address could wrongly let that happen. I'm weighing whether sync should define its own slot-aware key protocol or address type versus just parameterizing the registry with a `slot_of` callable that extracts the grouping key, which seems like the cleanest way to avoid duplicating the model's CredentialAddress logic.

Since Mapping is invariant in its key type, the port's read method needs to return Mapping[Address, Reading] rather than keyed by CredentialAddress directly, though a dict literal with CredentialAddress keys should still satisfy that annotation. One wrinkle: once a key comes back typed as the plain Address tuple, accessing it like `.user_ref` won't type-check anymore, so code would need to unpack or index into it instead, which is a bit awkward.

I'm weighing whether to keep the key type generic versus specific, thinking about where keys get used—dict keys, sorting, logging, and ownership lookups via the slot index. I consider having sync define its own NamedTuple Address type, but subclassing CredentialAddress across layers feels wrong since model shouldn't depend on sync even if it's technically allowed, and the reverse import direction doesn't work either since sync can't import from model.

I lean toward a generic-free tuple alias for Address in sync, with HA passing in its own CredentialAddress NamedTuple that satisfies the shape—though I'm checking whether reconstructing CredentialAddress from the plain tuple loses type precision on the credential type field, which nudges me back toward considering a bounded generic approach instead.

Weighing the trade-off, I keep coming back to the user's stated preference for simplicity over type plumbing, so the honest answer is probably just the plain tuple alias in sync with CredentialAddress as a subtype used wherever HA needs more structure.

Renaming the fields would touch providers/_base, binary_sensor, and roughly ten other call sites, but since slot_num stays an int identity there's no real split needed. I'm leaning toward moving the address type down into sync as a generic NamedTuple, though typing kind as a plain str would lose the CredentialType information, which pushes me toward making it generic over K with a Hashable bound so the port and worker types line up.

PEP 695's bound syntax can't reference another type parameter in the same list, so I can't express the port's bound in terms of the worker's key type directly -- I'd need to drop the generic port parameter or type it loosely as LockPort[Any], which feels messy.     True once it is done, False once the lock has refused or the slot is
    held after its tries; None if it is still going when the wait runs out
    (the lock is backing off), and it carries on.
    """

    done = asyncio.Event()

    @callback
    def _check() -> None:
        if slot not in worker.slots or worker.slots[slot].hold is not None:
            done.set()

        _check()
        async with asyncio.timeout(WRITE_ONCE_WAIT):

    hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str, worker: LockWorker[ProviderPort]

    Raise a repair for each slot the worker holds, and drop resolved ones.

    A slot it could not set is ``slot_suspended``; a clear that would not
    take is ``slot_clear_failed`` -- the code may still open the door. A
    refused PIN turns the slot off through ``on_disable`` instead. A lock
    that answered before and has stopped answering is ``lock_offline``.

    given_up = data[GIVEN_UP_KEY]
    for key, (_, clearing) in list(given_up.items()):
        if (
            key[0] == lock_entity_id
            and clearing is worker
            and key[1] not in worker.slots

    # worker's to resolve: its repair stays until it is tried again.

            owner is not None
            and slot.want is not None
            and worker.status(slot_num)[0] is Status.IN_SYNC

            owner.entry_id
            if owner is not None

            continue

        raised.add(issue_id)
        translation_key, reason = issue
        provider = worker.port.provider
        # A cause the provider named, alone: the link's counters would point
        # away from it. Otherwise the driver's own words over ours when it
        # would not set the code (#1398) -- a refused clear's are about
        # setting, and mislead -- then whatever the provider can measure of

            hass,
            DOMAIN,
            issue_id,
            is_fixable=True,
            is_persistent=True,
            severity=IssueSeverity.WARNING,
            translation_key=translation_key,
            translation_placeholders={
                "lock_entity_id": lock_entity_id,
                "lock_name": provider.display_name or lock_entity_id,
                "slot_num": str(slot_num),
                "reason": reason,

            # Persisted with the repair: after a restart, acknowledging it
            # still knows whose slot it was and that it was on its way out.

                "slot": slot_num,
                "entry_id": entry_id,
                "release": slot.release,

            hass,
            DOMAIN,
            offline_issue,
            is_fixable=False,
            is_persistent=True,
            severity=IssueSeverity.WARNING,
            translation_key="lock_offline",
            translation_placeholders={"lock_entity_id": lock_entity_id},

async def async_resume_slot(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    lock_entity_id: str,
    slot: int,
    *,
    entry_id: str | None = None,
    release: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """
    Try a held slot again: the user acknowledged its repair.

    A clear given up on a lock no entry holds any more has no worker left;
    it is started over as a one-off clear -- a release still. ``entry_id``
    and ``release`` come from the repair, which outlives a restart where
    what was remembered of the slot does not.
    """
    worker = lock_registry(hass).worker(lock_entity_id)
    if worker is not None and slot in worker.slots:
        worker.resume(slot)
        return
    given_up = hass.data[DATA][GIVEN_UP_KEY]
    key = (lock_entity_id, slot)
    if key not in given_up and release and entry_id is not None:
        given_up[key] = (entry_id, None)

        worker = await lock_registry(hass).write_once(
            lock_entity_id,
            slot,
            None,
            # Still a release: a native-user lock deletes the user it tagged.
            before=lambda new: _begin_release(hass, new.port, slot),

        given_up[key] = (given_up[key][0], worker)

    """Make ``slot``'s next clear on ``port`` a release, saying if LCM wrote a PIN there."""

    port.release(
        slot,
        written=store is not None and store.wrote_pin(port.provider.lock.id, slot),
    )


def _label(reading: Reading) -> str | SlotCode:
    """Return a reading as the views are told it: its PIN, or what the lock said."""
    if isinstance(reading, Holds):
        return reading.pin
    return {
        Seen.EMPTY: SlotCode.EMPTY,
        Seen.MASKED: SlotCode.UNREADABLE_CODE,
        Seen.SILENT: SlotCode.UNANSWERED,
        Seen.DISABLED: SlotCode.DISABLED,
    }[reading]


@callback
def lock_codes(hass: HomeAssistant, lock_entity_id: str) -> dict[int, str | SlotCode]:
    """
    Return every code the lock has told of: managed slots and the rest.

    What the lock said, never the PIN a slot wants: a card stands the
    configured PIN in for a slot in sync itself, marked as configured rather
    than read (spec D, #1282).

    A managed slot without a reading is never shown by an older word in
    ``port.others``: that may be the very reading set aside to read the slot
    again (``Slot.doubt``). On a lock that has answered it is being checked,
    as its per-lock entities say; before then it is left out.
    """
    if (worker := lock_registry(hass).worker(lock_entity_id)) is None:
        return {}
    not_reported = worker.port.not_reported

    def _label_of(slot: int, reading: Reading) -> str | SlotCode:
        if slot in not_reported and reading in (Seen.SILENT, Seen.MASKED):
            return SlotCode.NOT_REPORTED
        return _label(reading)

    codes = {
        slot: _label_of(slot, reading) for slot, reading in worker.port.others.items()
    }
    for slot_num, slot in worker.slots.items():
        if slot.seen is not None:
            codes[slot_num] = _label_of(slot_num, slot.seen)
        elif not slot.release:
            if worker.answered:
                codes[slot_num] = SlotCode.CHECKING
            else:
                codes.pop(slot_num, None)
    return codes

    worker: LockWorker[ProviderPort], *, forget_reporting: bool = False
) -> None:
    """
    Re-read the whole lock, past any cache, in its turn: the hard refresh service.

    The probe brings a lock that is backing off back; the provider's unscoped
    hard refresh re-reads every slot (codes nobody here manages included);
    the read after it brings what it found into view.

    ``forget_reporting`` first stops taking the lock for one that can report
    its codes (#1581): a write-only lock that once seemed to describe a slot
    has every slot it cannot tell of taken for good otherwise. Only asked
    for: a lock that can report shows it again only at a read that describes
    a slot, and the slots read here are its own, which may describe none.
    """
    provider = worker.port.provider
    if forget_reporting:
        worker.port.reports.pop(provider.lock.id, None)
        if (store := provider.hass.data.get(DATA, {}).get(STORE_KEY)) is not None:
            store.unreported(provider.lock.id)
    await worker.read(probe=True)

    async def _walk() -> None:
        try:
            await provider.async_hard_refresh_codes()
        except LockCodeManagerProviderError as err:
            if (error := lock_error(err, clearing=False)) is None:
                raise
            raise error from err

    await worker.turn(_walk)
    await worker.read()
